title: Traits
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Interfaces

C# interfaces describe instance contracts; combine with **`switch` expressions** on types for polymorphic dispatch.

exercises.title: Trait for struct
exercises.description: `trait Shape { fn area(&self)->f64 }` for `Rectangle { w,h }` — print area of 3×4.

exercises.title: std::io::Write
exercises.description: Implement `Write` for a `Logger` that prints the byte length and the UTF-8 payload on one line, like `5 hello` (same idea as Go’s `fmt.Print(n, " ", string(b))`).

exercises.title: Two shapes
exercises.description: Circle and rectangle implement `Shape`; print larger area for r=5 and 3×4.

exercises.title: Trait object accessor
exercises.description: `trait Describable { fn name(&self) -> &str; }` implemented by `Person`; print name via `dyn Describable`.

exercises.title: enum dispatch
exercises.description: C# prefers enums over `interface{{}}`; model `int` / `string` arms and print like the Go type switch.

exercises.title: enum of variants
exercises.description: Same as Go empty-interface slice: use `enum Item` with `Int`, `Str`, `Float` and `match`.
